---
title: "Papers and citation"
description: "The manuscripts behind the three packages, and how to cite them."
---

Each package has a methods paper that states its scope and its limits more
carefully than documentation can. If you use a package in published work, please
cite the paper where one is available, and the package otherwise.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Publication status changes. Check each package's `citation()` output in R for
the current, authoritative reference — that is what gets updated on release.

``` r
citation("splitGraph")
citation("bioLeak")
citation("fastml")
```
:::

## splitGraph

**splitGraph: A validatable, cross-language representation of dataset dependency
structure for leakage-aware evaluation**

Selcuk Korkmaz. Department of Biostatistics, Trakya University, Edirne, Turkey.

Prepared for the *Journal of Open Source Software*. The manuscript source is in
[`paper.md`](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/splitGraph/blob/main/paper.md) in
the package repository.

The argument: split correctness is currently re-litigated inside every tool that
resamples, in that tool's own vocabulary. A validatable, serialisable
representation of dataset structure lets the question be answered once and
checked independently — including across languages.

## bioLeak

**bioLeak: Leakage-Aware Modeling and Diagnostics for Machine Learning in R**

Selcuk Korkmaz. Department of Biostatistics, Trakya University, Edirne, Turkey.

Prepared in *Journal of Statistical Software* format. The manuscript source,
simulation scripts, and case study are under
[`paper/`](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/bioLeak/tree/main/paper) in the
package repository.

The argument: leakage-aware resampling is necessary but not sufficient. Once
folds are clean you still need evidence about what remains — permutation gaps,
batch association, target-leakage scans — and that evidence should be produced
by the same machinery that produced the estimate.

## fastml

**fastml: Guarded Resampling Workflows for Safer Automated Machine Learning in R**

Selcuk Korkmaz, Dincer Goksuluk, Eda Karaismailoglu.

Prepared in *R Journal* format. The manuscript source is under
[`RJ/`](https://github.com/selcukorkmaz/fastml/tree/main/RJ) in the package
repository.

The argument: AutoML tools compete on model search while leaving the evaluation
design to the user, which is where the errors actually are. Constraining the
workflow so that preprocessing cannot escape the resampling loop removes a whole
class of user-induced error at no statistical cost.

## Citing the family

There is no paper for the collection, because there is no package for the
collection — see [why](index.qmd#why-there-is-no-guardedverse-package). Cite the
packages you actually used.

If you are describing the overall approach in a methods section, the honest
phrasing is something like:

> Dataset dependency structure was encoded and validated with **splitGraph**
> [ref], leakage-resistant resampling and post-hoc leakage auditing were
> performed with **bioLeak** [ref], and model training and comparison used
> **fastml** [ref] with the resampling scheme fixed upstream.

The last clause matters: it is the part a reader cannot verify from the usual
methods boilerplate, and it is the part that makes the rest meaningful.
